title: One missed patch and this test launches the real provider
what: The test stubs shutil.which and create_subprocess_exec by string path, with no marker and no skip.
why: [Assumption] If the orchestrator moves the which call to another module the patch target stops matching, the real CLI is found, and a plain verify run bills a provider.
fix: In cli/tests/conftest.py add an autouse fixture that sets PATH to an empty temp dir for every test not marked llm, so a slipped patch fails instead of billing.

title: Deleting a schedule cancels it and no test says so
what: destroy sets status to CANCELED instead of deleting the row; no test under tests/ calls DELETE on /schedules/.
why: A refactor that drops the override back to the default destroy hard-deletes schedules and their run history with every test green.
fix: Add test_delete_schedule_cancels in backend/tests/test_x.py: DELETE /schedules/<id>/ returns 204 and the row still exists with status CANCELED.

title: The user list test passes on any two rows
what: The test checks the result count and never reads a name, email or ordering.
why: A serializer that drops the email field, or a queryset that returns the wrong users, keeps the count at two and the test green.
fix: Assert the two emails come back in the expected order and that each row carries name and email.

title: Five cost tests are red in both runs
what: Both runs of the verify gate's snapshots suite end with the same five cost failures in this file.
why: The suite is red, so nobody reads its result, and a real snapshot regression lands in the same output nobody reads.
fix: Re-capture the snapshot with the workspace's snapshot extractor tool so the pricing table matches, then assert the five tests pass.
